summary.headline: G R Infra Q1 FY27 standalone revenue rose 32.71% YoY to ~INR2,423 crores, but standalone EBITDA margin fell to 11.02% from 12.65%.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue grew 32.71% YoY to about INR2,423 crores, while consolidated revenue rose 40% to INR2,784 crores. Margins compressed on higher construction and material costs, with standalone EBITDA margin at 11.02% versus 12.65% a year earlier and group EBITDA margin at 16.8% versus 20%. Management kept FY27 standalone revenue growth guidance at 15-20% despite the 30%+ first-quarter run-rate, citing appointed-date timing for new projects. Order book stands at about INR25,300 crores as of 1 July 2026, with about INR32,000 crores of bids yet to be opened.

segments.name: Transport (highways and surface transport)
segments.commentary: Main growth driver in Q1 per management; the INR28,000 crore 'road' pipeline bid-out figure includes metro and other surface transport.

segments.name: Power transmission and distribution (T&D)
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR110 crores versus about INR75 crores in the prior quarter; company is setting up tower manufacturing and expanding that facility.

segments.name: Oil and gas
segments.commentary: Q1 revenue about INR270 crores; FY27 target above INR1,000 crores. Two projects currently in the books, with external receivables elevated until completion around May 2027.

segments.name: Warehousing
segments.commentary: Capital deployed to date about INR130 crores; FY27 plan INR450-500 crores.

segments.name: BharatNet
segments.commentary: FY27 expected revenue about INR400 crores, of which about INR300 crores is capex (cabling, starting second half) and the balance O&M. Order book about INR1,000 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 standalone revenue growth guided at 15-20%; management said 25% is possible if appointed dates arrive by October-December.
FY28 revenue target about INR11,000-12,000 crores assuming about 20% growth, with margins in a similar range.
Standalone EBITDA margin guided at 10-11% for the current scenario.
FY27 order inflow target about INR20,000-22,000 crores (plus-minus 10%), with road about INR14,000 crores.
FY27 capex about INR300 crores; FY28 capex INR200-250 crores.
Other income expected to continue at the Q1 run rate for the next three quarters.
Around three to four assets targeted for transfer to the InvIT in FY27.
Equity contribution to HAM/BoT projects: INR900-1,000 crores in FY27; about INR3,300 crores over the next three years.
capex_capacity: Standalone net block of PP&E INR1,019 crores at June 2026; Q1 additions INR22 crores.
Investments in subsidiaries INR2,445 crores (loans and equity) at June 2026; balance HAM/BoT equity commitment INR3,346 crores.
Appointed dates awaited for three projects worth INR7,250 crores. Agra-Gwalior expected October-November 2026; two other HAM projects targeted for December 2026.
BharatNet capex awaiting right-of-way; capex expected to start around October 2026.
BESS work under way; battery procurement pending a move in FX and geopolitical conditions, expected within about three months.
Railway project in MP already started; management said no more than about 15% execution in year one.
Tower manufacturing facility being expanded to address tower supply delays.
demand_pricing: Pipeline cited at about INR3.85 lakh crores in transport (78% highway, 16% railway, 6% metro); government proposes a toll-cum-annuity model with 10-25% upfront support and a 20-year concession.
Government approved multi-tracking projects worth about INR48,000 crores in the quarter.
Bitumen cost spike is compensated by a government circular over and above escalation clauses; diesel and energy cost increases are not compensated, hitting margins.
Power transmission contracts have no escalation; aluminium and copper price spikes hit margins, expected to normalise over 3-6 months and spread over about two years.
Management expects road competition to ease as project sizes grow and BOT participation narrows to strong balance sheets; railway freight corridors may move to HAM.
Order inflow to date has lagged government pipeline claims for about two years, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 guidance still 15% revenue growth after 32% in Q1, and what about FY28 margins?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 guidance kept at 15-20%; FY28 growth could approach 20%. Margin range 10-11% for now, with possible marginal improvement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the split of the INR32,000 crore bids yet to open, and is INR20,000-25,000 crore inflow achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Road/transport about INR28,000 crores and hydro and tunnels about INR4,000 crores. Management said FY27 inflow target of about INR20,000-22,000 crores is achievable, with road around INR14,000 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Why was other income low in Q1 and what is the InvIT distribution?
qa_highlights.answer: InvIT payment was partly capital repayment, which hits the balance sheet, not P&L. Total other income about INR68 crores, of which INR20 crores from InvIT and INR35 crores other interest. InvIT distribution about INR70 crores in the quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why did trade receivables rise and when will they unwind?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly oil and gas receivables; collection expected as projects complete, with the current project finishing around May 2027.

qa_highlights.question: How is raw material inflation handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Bitumen is compensated by government circular over escalation. Diesel is not, and power transmission has no escalation, so margins are impacted in the near term.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company pursuing international or Middle East opportunities?
qa_highlights.answer: No international focus for the next 1-2 years; domestic credentials first, with international possibly after about one year.

qa_highlights.question: How will the large equity and InvIT value be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management plans BOT projects, transmission and logistics to deploy accrued cash at meaningful returns; said it is waiting for suitable opportunities.

risks_watch: Appointed dates still awaited for three projects worth INR7,250 crores (Agra-Gwalior, two HAM projects); management targets October-December 2026, and FY27 growth above 20% depends on them.

Margin pressure from diesel and energy costs (not compensated) and aluminium/copper spikes in power transmission (no escalation); management expects normalisation over 3-6 months with cost spread over about two years.
Trade receivables at INR2,655 crores standalone (INR1,784 crores HAM debtors) and working capital days up to 148 from 128; oil and gas receivables linger until the project completes around May 2027.

Road order inflow has lagged government pipeline claims for about two years; FY27 inflow target of INR20,000-22,000 crores depends on bids opening, with the INR32,000 crore pending bid pool mostly road.

BharatNet capex awaits right-of-way (expected around October 2026), and OFC cost increases are unrecoverable under a fixed-price vendor contract; BESS battery procurement depends on FX and geopolitics.
Capital deployment of large equity and InvIT proceeds into BOT, transmission and logistics remains unspecified; management is 'waiting for right opportunities'.

summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the order book, Q1 execution and the medium-term pipeline, but cautious on FY27 guidance, keeping revenue growth at 15-20% despite a 30%+ first quarter. It was also cautious on margins (10-11% range) because of diesel, energy and metal cost inflation, and was vague on how it will deploy surplus cash and when road ordering will actually convert.
